w_p1: HomePad is a launcher for your Mac: press a shortcut and a panel opens with a search bar and your apps, in categories you choose. It can replace the Dock.
w_p2: This installer puts HomePad in your Applications folder and opens it. It takes less than a minute.
w_li1: Click Continue through the next screens, then Install. Your Mac asks for your password once.
w_li2: HomePad opens by itself and shows its own welcome window, which asks for three permissions. The next screen explains them.
w_muted: Needs macOS 13 (Ventura) or newer. Works on Apple silicon and Intel Macs.
r_p: After installing, HomePad's welcome window asks for three permissions. Each one is optional, but HomePad works best with all three. Nothing is recorded, saved or sent anywhere.
r_sr_h: Screen Recording: previews of your windows
r_sr_1: Click the red Allow… button. A message with a padlock appears.
r_sr_2: Click Open System Settings in that message.
r_sr_3: Turn on the switch next to HomePad, then click Quit & Reopen. HomePad restarts by itself.
r_ax_h: Accessibility: jump to a window, and the double-tap shortcut
r_ax_1: Click Allow…, then Open System Settings in the padlock message.
r_ax_2: Turn on the switch next to HomePad. The welcome window comes back by itself.
r_fda_h: Full Disk Access: search in Documents, Desktop and Downloads
r_fda_1: Click Allow… and System Settings opens, with a small HomePad window beside it.
r_fda_2: Turn on the switch next to HomePad. If it isn't in the list, drag the icon from the small window into the list first. Then click Quit & Reopen.
r_end: Then choose how to open HomePad (the standard shortcut is Option-Space) and click Get started.
c_p: HomePad is in your Applications folder, and it is opening now. Follow its welcome window to give it the three permissions you just read about.
c_use: Press Option-Space to open HomePad and press it again to close it, or click the grid icon in the menu bar at the top of the screen. Right-click that icon for Settings, the language and to quit.
c_trash_h: If your Mac can't move the installer to the Trash
c_trash: That happens when an earlier HomePad-Installer.dmg is already in the Trash. It's harmless: click OK, then delete HomePad-Installer.dmg from Downloads.
d_subtitle: HomePad isn't from the App Store, so your Mac stops the installer once. To let it through:
d_step2: A message says it can't be opened. Click **Done** (not Move to Trash).
d_step3: Double-click the blue button below. In the page that opens, scroll to the bottom and click **Open Anyway**.
d_step4: Confirm with **Open Anyway** and your password. The installer opens: click **Continue**, then **Install**.
d_footnote: On macOS 13 or 14 it's quicker: right-click the installer, choose **Open**, then **Open** again.
